text:
incident-bot: SEV2 alert: GPU queue > 600 pending requests on prod-ml-cluster for 7m. Autoscaler failing to add GPU nodes. Paging oncall. :rotating_light:

ashok: saw it, thanks. any error logs from the autoscaler?

maria: metrics look nasty — token gen queue spiking, 95th latency > 4s. Failed requests increased. customers hitting rate limits.

kevin: pulling autoscaler logs now (`kubectl -n kube-system logs deploy/cluster-autoscaler`).

kevin: log excerpt:
```
I0323 14:02:11.123456 1 scale_up.go:512] No candidates for scale up: no nodes in node groups match the requested GPU launch template
E0323 14:02:12.223456 1 scale_up.go:634] Failed to increase ASG desired capacity: AccessDenied: User: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:user/autoscaler cannot call: autoscaling:SetDesiredCapacity
status code: 403, request id: a1b2c3d4
```

lina: so two issues: 1) launch-template mismatch (new GPUs requested don't match any nodegroup), 2) IAM denied SetDesiredCapacity.

oncall-eu: paging ops-team now. @infra-eng can you confirm if we recently rolled any launch template changes?

infra-eng: we rolled a minor AMI bump to gpu-node-launch-v3 yesterday for spot optimization. Looks like some nodegroups still reference v2. The autoscaler is requesting nodes with label `accelerator=nvidia-a100` and launch template v3 metadata; v2 nodegroups don't accept that.

ashok: and the IAM error? autoscaler role shouldn't be hitting 403 unless policies were changed. @devops-bot can you check IAM policy diff?

devops-bot: detected policy change: `autoscaler-assume-role` had `autoscaling:SetDesiredCapacity` removed in policy edit at 11:07 UTC (who: infra-deploy). Rolling back change now. :gear:

pagerduty-bot: On-call (US) notified: oncall-us has been paged.

oncall-us: I'm on it. patching can wait, immediate mitigation first — we need to get capacity up now. Options: manual ASG resize, launch emergency on-demand nodes, or temporarily route low-priority traffic to secondary cluster.

maria: customer-impact assessment: at least 3 high-value customers reporting degraded responses; internal KPIs show token throughput down ~40%. Recommend declaring customer-impacting incident and notify CS. :exclamation:

customer-success: alerted customers with templated notice; will send an update after mitigation.

kevin: attempting manual ASG increase as interim: `aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name rg-gpu-prod --desired-capacity 12 --honor-cooldown false`

kevin: error from AWS CLI: `You are not authorized to perform this operation.` Same 403.

ashok: autoscaler role rollback still in progress. expected completion in ~2 mins. Meanwhile we can try manual node boot: launch an EC2 instance with correct launch template and AMI, join cluster with kubelet. Who can do quick manual?

lina: I can spin up a node in us-east-1a with launch-template gpu-node-launch-v3. Doing it now. I'll annotate it `manual-ephemeral-713`.

infra-eng: FYI autoscaler is also refusing to schedule because new nodegroup has taint `dedicated=gpu:NoSchedule` and pods are not tolerating it; the runtime creates GPU Pods without tolerations. That explains the "no candidates" message. We need to either remove the taint or patch pods to tolerate.

maria: can we temporarily remove taint on the manually created node?

lina: yes. once node is up I'll `kubectl taint nodes manual-ephemeral-713 dedicated=gpu:NoSchedule-` to remove taint.

kevin: autoscaler policy rollback complete — IAM `SetDesiredCapacity` restored. scaling via ASG now allowed.

kevin: triggered ASG desired capacity to 12 and increased max to 20 to allow burst: `aws autoscaling update-auto-scaling-group --auto-scaling-group-name rg-gpu-prod --max-size 20 --desired-capacity 12` — succeeded. :white_check_mark:

devops-bot: note: we should track who changed autoscaler policy; tagging infra-deploy for postmortem.

lina: manual node booted and joined cluster. removed taint. `kubectl get nodes` shows manual-ephemeral-713 Ready, gpu allocatable 80Gi.

ashok: redeploying a couple of pending workloads to schedule onto new capacity (`kubectl -n ml-prod rollout restart deploy/llm-workers`) to drain queue.

maria: queue length dropping from 620 -> 210 in 6 minutes. 95th latency back to 1.2s. Customers report improvements.

oncall-us: updating incident to SEV2 with customer impact. Notifying Support and Product.

customer-success: telling customers we have mitigation in place and are restoring capacity; ETA for stable: 30m.

infra-eng: follow-up items we need to capture:
- reconcile launch template versions across nodegroups (v2/v3 drift)
- ensure autoscaler requests compatible nodegroup labels/launch templates
- revert/remove taints or add tolerations for runtime pods where appropriate
- restrict IAM edits to a small set and add CI guardrails
- add alerting for autoscaler IAM failures

ashok: agree. owner for postmortem: ashok (infra). timeline lead: kevin. CS follow-up: maria.

kevin: starting incident retrospective doc in /incidents/postmortems and assigning runbook edits to infra team.

oncall-eu: handing off to oncall-us for the follow-up watch window (30m). oncall-us ack.

incident-bot: incident update: Mitigated — manual and ASG scale-up added 6 GPU nodes; queue decreasing; monitoring for 30m. Incident channel will remain open for postmortem notes. :lock_with_ink_pen:

maria: thanks team. I'll send an initial customer update in 10m, then a detailed postmortem within 48h.

customer-success: noted. closing customer-facing message after internal doc posted.

ashok: logging timeline and artifacts. attaching autoscaler logs, IAM diff, and ASG events to the incident doc.

kevin: last check: pending queue 38, token throughput at 95% baseline. leaving watch.

oncall-us: watch window started. will escalate if queue > 150 again.

infra-eng: creating Jira: INFRA-8142 "Launch template drift causing autoscaler failures" and linking to incident.

maria: closing incident channel for now — will re-open if any regressions. Good job everyone. :clap:
